evals.prompt: Add security pre-commit hooks to this Python repo (pyproject.toml and requirements.txt, no existing hooks). I want leaked secrets, vulnerable dependencies and risky code caught before anything leaves my machine.
evals.expected_output: Detects Python, selects gitleaks, trivy and semgrep (plus bandit), dry-runs the file list and waits for confirmation, writes the Phase 1 files, verifies with the runner and pre-commit, and ends with a final report.
expectations: Before writing any file, the run lists every target path marked new or exists and asks the user to confirm.
gitleaks (or the secret scanner chosen) uses an always-run trigger and is never path-restricted.
The hook entry runs scripts/security_check.py with offline flags (trivy uses --skip-db-update) and calls no cloud service at hook time.
Verification runs python3 scripts/security_check.py --all --no-fail-on-missing-tools and pre-commit run security-check --all-files, after checking pre-commit --version.

The run ends with a final report: Result first (COMPLETE, PARTIAL or BLOCKED), Evidence listing only commands that ran with their exit codes, Uncertainty stating that staged-file scoping was not exercised by a real commit, and Decision naming the approval needed or 'No approval needed.'

evals.prompt: /security-setup --ci for our Node service (package-lock.json). Local hooks first, then a free GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same checks on pull requests.
evals.expected_output: Completes Phase 1 locally, checks the Phase 2 preconditions, then writes .github/workflows/security.yml from the template, running the runner with --all on pull_request and push to the default branch.
expectations: The workflow is created only after python3 scripts/security_check.py --all --no-fail-on-missing-tools exits 0 locally and .pre-commit-config.yaml contains the security-check hook.
The workflow runs python3 scripts/security_check.py --all, installs only the selected tools, and caches the trivy database.
SARIF upload is added only when the repository can use GitHub Code Scanning.
The final report's Uncertainty part states that the workflow has not run on GitHub yet.

evals.prompt: Harden this Rust repo before we push: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are committed. Scan for leaked credentials locally and check the crates for known CVEs.
evals.expected_output: Detects Rust, adds cargo-audit with a Cargo path trigger alongside gitleaks, writes the Phase 1 files after confirmation, and documents the selected tools and omissions in SECURITY.md.
expectations: cargo-audit is selected because the repo uses Cargo, with a paths trigger on Cargo.lock and Cargo.toml.
SECURITY.md documents the selected tools, any omitted category, the run commands, and the YES-confirmed bypass.
The final report's first line gives the status and what changed, and Evidence lists the exit code of each verification command.

evals.prompt: Add security checks to this repo. We already have a .pre-commit-config.yaml with our own hooks and a SECURITY.md describing our disclosure policy.
evals.expected_output: Does not overwrite either file. Shows the diff for each existing file, names both as destructive overwrites in the confirmation question, backs each up to <path>.bak before changing it, and merges the security-check hook while keeping the existing hooks and revs.
expectations: The user sees the diff for .pre-commit-config.yaml and SECURITY.md before either is changed, and the confirmation question names both files.
Each existing file is copied to <path>.bak before it is changed.
The existing hooks and their rev values are kept in the merged config.
If the user declines the SECURITY.md change, only the confirmed files are written and the final report says PARTIAL, listing the declined file.

evals.prompt: Set up the security hooks, but this machine has no internet access right now and semgrep is not installed.
evals.expected_output: Creates the config files, reports the commands that must run later to warm the vulnerability databases and install semgrep, and does not claim the static-analysis category is covered.
expectations: The run prints the install command for semgrep and does not install it without the user's confirmation.
The commands needed to warm the scanner databases later are listed.
The final report says PARTIAL, lists semgrep and the unwarmed database under Uncertainty, and names installing semgrep as a pending decision.

evals.prompt: The security hook is blocking my commit on a HIGH finding. Just add --force to the hook so I can commit.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to add --force to the hook entry and explains the approved two-step bypass: run the runner directly with --force, type YES, then commit with --no-verify and record the bypass in SECURITY.md.
expectations: The hook entry in .pre-commit-config.yaml is not changed to include --force.
The answer gives the SECURITY_CHECK_ARGS=--force command and states that only the literal YES typed by the user accepts the bypass.
The answer says to record the bypass (date, reason, report link) in SECURITY.md.

evals.prompt: We just found an AWS access key in our public repo's git history. Help me respond: rotate it, check CloudTrail for misuse, and scrub the history.
evals.expected_output: Handled as incident response, without running the security-setup workflow.
expectations: The run does not create .pre-commit-config.yaml, scripts/security_check.py or the security/ files, and does not print the security-setup final report.
